studies.Reference: Wine and other alcohol consumption and risk of ovarian cancer in the California Teachers Study cohort.
studies.Authors: Chang ET, Canchola AJ, Lee VS, Clarke CA, Purdie DM, Reynolds P, Bernstein L, Stram DO, Anton-Culver H, Deapen D, Mohrenweiser H, Peel D, Pinder R, Ross RK, West DW, Wright W, Ziogas A, Horn-Ross PL
studies.comparison_type: At least one glass per day of wine vs no wine
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Consumption of total alcohol, beer, or liquor in the year prior to baseline, at ages 30-35 years, or at ages 18-22 years was assessed.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Among 90,371 eligible members of the California Teachers Study cohort.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Consumption of at least one glass per day of wine was associated with increased risk of developing ovarian cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: 253 women were diagnosed with epithelial ovarian cancer by the end of 2003.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Consumption of total alcohol, beer, or liquor in the year prior to baseline, at ages 30-35 years, or at ages 18-22 years was assessed.

studies.Reference: Alcohol intake and ovarian cancer risk: a pooled analysis of 10 cohort studies.
studies.Authors: Genkinger JM, Hunter DJ, Spiegelman D, Anderson KE, Buring JE, Freudenheim JL, Goldbohm RA, Harnack L, Hankinson SE, Larsson SC, Leitzmann M, McCullough ML, Marshall J, Miller AB, Rodriguez C, Rohan TE, Schatzkin A, Schouten LJ, Wolk A, Zhang SM, Smith-Warner SA
studies.Stage: Epithelial (includes endometrioid, mucinous, and serous subtypes)
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Alcohol intake was measured in grams per day.

extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: no associations were observed for intakes of total alcohol.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: 2001 incident epithelial ovarian cases were documented.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: intakes of total alcohol (pooled multivariate RR=1.12, 95% CI 0.86-1.44 comparing > or =30 to 0 g day(-1) of alcohol).

studies.Reference: Association of folate and alcohol with risk of ovarian cancer in a prospective study of postmenopausal women.
studies.Authors: Kelemen LE, Sellers TA, Vierkant RA, Harnack L, Cerhan JR
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Dietary folate and alcohol intakes and lifestyle and medical information were collected with self-administered questionnaires in 1986.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Among 27,205 eligible women free of baseline cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Compared to non-drinkers, the RRs for increasing alcohol intake were 1.0 (referent), 0.78 for 0.01-3.9 g/d, 0.75 for 4.0-9.9 g/d and 0.58 for > or =10 g/d.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: These findings suggest that alcohol consumption is inversely related to postmenopausal ovarian cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: 147 incident epithelial ovarian cancer cases were identified by linkage to a cancer registry.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Dietary folate and alcohol intakes and lifestyle and medical information were collected with self-administered questionnaires.

studies.Reference: Alcohol and ovarian cancer risk: results from the Netherlands Cohort Study.
studies.Authors: Schouten LJ, Zeegers MP, Goldbohm RA, van den Brandt PA
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: A self-administered questionnaire on dietary habits and other risk factors for cancer was completed.

extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The RRs of ovarian cancer for women who consumed >15 g of alcohol per day were 0.92.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: These data do not suggest a major association between alcohol intake and ovarian cancer risk.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: 214 incident invasive epithelial ovarian cancer cases.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Alcohol consumption in the form of wine, beer or liquor.

studies.Reference: Evaluating the role of alcohol consumption in breast and ovarian cancer susceptibility using population-based cohort studies and two-sample Mendelian randomization analyses.
studies.Authors: Ong JS, Derks EM, Eriksson M, An J, Hwang LD, Easton DF, Pharoah PP, Berchuck A, Kelemen LE, Matsuo K, Chenevix-Trench G, Hall P, Bojesen SE, Webb PM, MacGregor S
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: The abstract does not provide enough information to determine whether the exposure was dietary intake or biospecimen-based.

extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: the multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios (HR) for a one standard drink/day increase was 1.00 (0.92, 1.08) for EOC
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Our data provide additional evidence that alcohol intake is unlikely to have anything other than a very small effect on risk of EOC.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: The association with epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) is unclear.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Alcohol consumption is correlated positively with risk for breast cancer in observational studies.

studies.Reference: Alcohol consumption and ovarian cancer risk.
studies.Authors: Gwinn ML, Webster LA, Lee NC, Layde PM, Rubin GL
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Women were asked about their consumption of alcoholic beverages during the previous five years.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 433 women 20-54 years of age with newly diagnosed ovarian cancer and 2,915 women 20-54 years of age selected at random.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Women who drank more than about 20 drinks per week had a relative risk of ovarian cancer of 0.5.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Women who drank more than about 20 drinks per week had a relative risk of ovarian cancer of 0.5.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: 433 women 20-54 years of age with newly diagnosed ovarian cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Women were asked about their consumption of alcoholic beverages during the previous five years.

studies.Reference: Alcohol consumption and ovarian cancer risk in a population-based case-control study.
studies.Authors: Peterson NB, Trentham-Dietz A, Newcomb PA, Chen Z, Hampton JM, Willett WC, Egan KM
studies.comparison_type: 1 drink/day or more vs none (beer, ages 20-30)
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Women reported their usual alcohol consumption as young adults (20-30 years of age) and in the recent past.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 762 incident cases of epithelial ovarian cancer and 6,271 population controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Regular drinking of beer (1 drink/day or more) during ages 20-30 (OR 1.55, 95% CI 1.07-2.26).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Regular drinking of beer during ages 20-30 was associated with a statistically significant increase in risk of invasive tumors.
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: p trend 0.42 (ages 20-30 years), p trend 0.83 (recent past).
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: 762 incident cases of epithelial ovarian cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Women reported their usual alcohol consumption as young adults (20-30 years of age) and in the recent past.

studies.Authors: La Vecchia C, Negri E, Franceschi S, Parazzini F, Gentile A, Fasoli M
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: This finding chiefly derived from an association between ovarian cancer risk and consumption of wine (which accounts for over 90% of alcohol intake in this female population).

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 801 histologically confirmed epithelial ovarian cancers and 2114 controls
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: 1.3 (95% CI 0.9 to 1.8) for three or more drinks per day
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: A significant direct trend in risk with dose emerged.

studies.Reference: Multivitamin and alcohol intake and folate receptor alpha expression in ovarian cancer.
studies.Authors: Kelemen LE, Sellers TA, Keeney GL, Lingle WL
studies.Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
studies.comparison_type: High alcohol intake (≥5 drinks/week) vs Low alcohol intake
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Weekly alcohol intake (≥5 drinks) was assessed.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Cases (n = 148) and controls (n = 148) were included in analyses.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: For alcohol, the associations were 0.84 (95% CI, 0.24-2.86) and 1.65 (95% CI, 0.69-3.93), respectively.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: The association for alcohol intake was reported as 1.65 for strong-expressing FRalpha tumors.

studies.Reference: Alcohol, wine, and risk of epithelial ovarian cancer.

studies.Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Information about diet and alcohol consumption was obtained from a food frequency questionnaire.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 696 Australian women with histologically confirmed epithelial ovarian cancer and 786 cancer-free control women.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Compared with nondrinkers, the OR for women who drank an average of > or =2 standard drinks/day was 0.49.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: These data suggest that alcohol does not increase risk of ovarian cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: 696 Australian women with histologically confirmed epithelial ovarian cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Information about diet and alcohol consumption was obtained from a food frequency questionnaire.

studies.Reference: Alcohol consumption and the risk of mucinous and nonmucinous epithelial ovarian cancer.
studies.Authors: Modugno F, Ness RB, Allen GO
studies.comparison_type: Current heavy alcohol consumption (24 g or more per day) vs None/Low
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: We examined total alcohol consumption and consumption of beer, wine, and spirits as risk factors.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 761 incident cases of epithelial ovarian cancer with 1352 community controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Current heavy alcohol consumption (24 g or more per day) was associated with mucinous (OR 1.93; 95% CI 1.02, 3.65).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Current heavy alcohol consumption might be a risk factor for mucinous epithelial ovarian cancer.

extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Total alcohol consumption and consumption of beer, wine, and spirits.

studies.Reference: Alcohol consumption and the risk of borderline and invasive ovarian cancer.
studies.Stage: Invasive tumors, especially endometrioid cell type
studies.comparison_type: Current drinkers consuming 14 or more drinks per week vs Never drinkers
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: In-person interviews were obtained regarding lifetime alcohol consumption.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: In-person interviews were obtained from 558 women with ovarian cancer and 607 population controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Current drinkers consuming 14 or more drinks per week had an OR of 0.36.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: The number of glasses of alcohol consumed on a weekly basis was inversely related to the OR for invasive ovarian cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Risk of ovarian cancer, specifically invasive tumors and endometrioid cell type.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Lifetime alcohol consumption, including beer, wine, and spirits.

studies.Reference: Alcohol consumption and risk of breast and ovarian cancer: A Mendelian randomization study.
studies.Authors: Zhu J, Jiang X, Niu Z
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: We examined three different alcohol intake exposures, drinks per week (drinks/week), alcohol use disorder (AUD) and age-adjusted alcohol use disorder identification test (AUDIT-C), to reflect the general and harmful drinking behavior.

studies.Reference: Alcohol intake and the risk of epithelial ovarian cancer.

studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Average alcohol intake over the lifetime and during specific age periods were computed from a detailed assessment of the intake of beer, red wine, white wine and spirits.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: In a population-based case-control study of 495 cases and 902 controls, conducted in Montreal, Canada.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: For each one drink/week increment in average alcohol intake over the lifetime, the adjusted OR (95% CI) was 1.06 (1.01-1.10) for ovarian cancer overall.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Our results support the hypothesis that a higher alcohol intake modestly increases the risk of overall ovarian cancer.

extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Dietary folate intake was associated with a 25% decrease in risk of ovarian cancer for the highest versus the lowest quartile level of intake (hazard ratio=0.75).

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger's test indicates no significant funnel plot asymmetry (p=0.1953). The distribution of studies appears symmetric, suggesting a lower risk of publication bias.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 19 studies yielded an effect size of 0.96 (95% CI: 0.87–1.07), indicating no statistically significant association between alcohol and ovarian cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by substantial heterogeneity (I² = 73.53%), reflecting considerable variability across studies.
